title: NdFeB process equipment and OEM evidence

coverage.scope: Illustrative documented OEM options, not installed equipment or customer/OEM contracts at a specific magnet factory.
unfilled: No directly verified magnet-specific coating-line OEM example in this review.
No site-metered machine-building factory electricity or full equipment bill of materials is disclosed in the inspected sources.

methodology.locationRule: Company nationality, headquarters, sales/service offices, processing sites, component manufacturing and final assembly are different claims.
methodology.powerRule: kW nameplate/output, kVA supply, amperes, stored-pulse joules and measured kWh are kept separate; no plant energy is derived automatically from OEM ratings.
methodology.specRule: Numerical specs apply only to the named configuration and listed source scope.
methodology.coordinates: City-centroid coordinates are approximate display anchors, not exact factory sites.
methodology.procurementRule: An OEM product example does not prove supply to any named magnet plant.

sources.title: ULVAC company profile and factory locations
claims: Head office and plant in Chigasaki; other listed factories do not establish the production location of a particular magnet-equipment model.

sources.title: ULVAC IR Seminar 2026 Q&A: melting-furnace production structure
claims: Chigasaki factory is being reconfigured for melting-furnace production; OEM says planned simultaneous assembly of four systems and twelve units per year. These are equipment factory capacities, not measured electricity.

sources.title: Industrial Furnaces for Magnets, Technical Journal 83E
claims: Magcaster-600 strip casting, FHH hydrogen treatment, FSC sintering, and Magrise grain-boundary diffusion explicitly address neodymium magnets. FHH hydrogen pressure up to 290 kPa absolute. Manufacturing-site mapping and operating kWh are absent.

sources.title: FMI Series / Magcaster vacuum induction melting furnaces
claims: FMI family lists NdFeB/SmCo applications and strip casting. FMI-1 standard Fe/Ni configuration: 5–100 kg melt, 25–100 kW output, 30–60 minutes melt, 3–12 t/h cooling water. Standard configuration ratings cannot be transferred directly to Magcaster or NdFeB batches.

sources.title: FSC Series vacuum sintering furnaces
claims: FSC inline vacuum sintering has rare-earth magnet applications; no published power rating on this product page.

sources.title: FHH-317 vacuum heat-treatment furnace
claims: FHH-317C: 1000 kg loading, 310×1300×1700 mm uniform zone, 1100 ±3 °C five-section heating uniformity; magnet sintering application listed. No rated kW.

sources.title: ULVAC thermal process applications
claims: Magcaster, FSC and FHH families are offered for melting, hydrogen processing, sintering and aging neodymium magnets; family applicability is not a specific FHH-317 aging recipe.

sources.title: ULVAC Environment-Oriented Products: magnet process equipment
claims: Generic magnet-process illustration gives vacuum dehydrogenation around 600 °C, sintering around 1100 °C and aging around 500 °C. These are illustrative process temperatures, not every model's operating recipe.

sources.title: Consarc Corporation February construction update
claims: Manufacturing expansion at Rancocas, New Jersey, is explicitly related to neodymium magnet VIM-SC strip-casting furnace capacity.

sources.title: Consarc Corp. company and product profile
claims: Consarc designs and manufactures VIM-SC and other vacuum furnaces; US corporate location is Rancocas.

sources.title: Consarc VIM brochure: US and UK engineering locations
claims: US and UK companies design vacuum-induction furnaces. UK address in Eurocentral establishes an office/engineering location, not model-specific VIM-SC assembly.

sources.title: Baiqida company profile and factory-development history
claims: Manufacturer of magnetic presses and hydrogen furnaces; factory completion in Ningbo Fenghua Binhai in 2014 and headquarters relocation in 2015. Baotou and Yantai subsidiaries are not automatically equipment-building sites.

sources.title: BQDHD rail-type hydrogen decrepitation furnace
claims: BQDHD-600GC: 600 kg per cylinder, ultimate vacuum 0.1 Pa, operating temperature ≤600 °C, inert-protected discharge, hydrogen absorption/dehydrogenation. Published page contains no heater kW.

sources.title: Baiqida laboratory hydrogen-decrepitation machine
claims: Lab system: 10 kg maximum load, 600 or 800 °C rated heating configuration, 0.1 MPa working pressure, vacuum dehydrogenation. Not production-scale throughput.

sources.title: Baiqida fully electric magnetic-field forming press
claims: DES-450 and BDES-600 tables list average 20 kW and maximum 120 kW; DES-450 field ≥2 T /60 mm. These are OEM equipment claims; duration, duty and measured plant kWh are not disclosed. Thick sealing plates and O-ring flanges are described.

sources.title: Baiqida forming-process solutions
claims: Magnetic pressing uses servo-electric or hydraulic actuation; OEM describes water-cooled coils and IGBT alignment/demagnetizing circuitry.

sources.title: Baiqida New Materials Service Center
claims: Ningbo, Baotou and Yantai are hydrogen-processing service bases. This does not prove magnet-equipment manufacturing in all three cities.

sources.title: Hosokawa Alpine rare-earth processing equipment
claims: AFG-R counter-jet mill explicitly processes NdFeB under sealed nitrogen/argon; particle target d50 below 3–5 µm; controlled passivation for opening.

sources.title: Jet milling for high-performance permanent magnets
claims: AFG-R system includes feeder, classifier, cyclone, dust filter, pressure tank and compressor; line scale up to 250 kg/h depends on configuration/material; Augsburg trials available.

sources.title: Hosokawa Alpine company and manufacturing
claims: Company develops and manufactures machines; Augsburg headquarters has production and assembly buildings. The brochure does not identify the assembly site of each shipped AFG-R.

sources.title: NETZSCH m-Jet high-density bed jet mill
claims: m-Jet explicitly designed for NdFeB magnetic powder dry fine grinding.

sources.title: NETZSCH rare-earth alloys application
claims: m-Jet integrates a dynamic classifier, uses inert grinding gas and rejects hard-to-grind components; no published compressor kW in this page.

sources.title: NETZSCH Trockenmahltechnik locations and activities
claims: Hanau is headquarters, development, application lab and toll-processing location. Stockach explicitly manufactures custom jet-nozzle hose filters. Hanau model-specific m-Jet assembly remains undisclosed.

sources.title: Nihon Denji Sokki magnetic-field press / RIP
claims: NdFeB rubber-isostatic press integrates powder fill, orientation, pressing and extraction. Published system has 100-ton press, pulsed field over 6.5 T, 200 V three-phase 150 A supply. Supply rating is not real kW.

sources.title: Nihon Denji Sokki EV magnetization and manufacturing
claims: Company states it develops and manufactures magnetic application equipment in Tachikawa, Tokyo; Shanghai and Bangkok are service/business hubs.

sources.title: Nihon Denji Sokki head office and factory contact
claims: Separate head office 8-59-2 Sunagawa-cho and factory 8-61-3 Sunagawa-cho, Tachikawa.

sources.title: Daxing MD7640 CNC double-disc magnet grinder
claims: MD7640 explicitly grinds NdFeB/SmCo/ferrite; two 11 kW grinding-head motors, 1–5 m/min feed. These are component motor ratings.

sources.title: Daxing automation and precision-grinding catalog
claims: MD7640: two 11 kW head motors, 0.55 kW feeder, resin-bond diamond grinding wheel 80–150 mesh. Catalog identifies Ningbo Yinzhou Daxing Non-standard Equipment Manufacturing Factory.

sources.title: Daxing manufacturing-factory contact
claims: Factory contact is Lishutang, Dongwu Town, Yinzhou District, Ningbo.

sources.title: Fengfan FFDXSG-4650 multi-wire cutter
claims: Diamond-wire cutting magnetic materials; maximum workpiece 160×650×160 mm. English page mixes 38 and 45 kW total-power variants; exact option mapping is unclear, so no power number is used.

sources.title: Fengfan company profile and production workshops
claims: Company locates CNC-machine production in Si'an, Changxing, Huzhou, Zhejiang, with plant/workshop descriptions. Chinese and English street addresses differ; only city-level location used.

sources.title: MAGNET-PHYSIK impulse magnetizers
claims: U-series 1400/2800 J systems typically magnetize NdFeB rotors approximately ≤60 mm; 2000 V charge, pulse current up to 60 kA. Joules per stored pulse are not continuous electrical load.

sources.title: MAGNET-PHYSIK company and regional roles
claims: German OEM's main contact is Cologne; China is explicitly sales-office representation. An inspected official page did not prove model assembly city.

sources.title: MAGNET-PHYSIK main company/contact
claims: Cologne head contact and calibration lab; USA sales/testing presence does not establish manufacturing.

sources.title: PERMAGRAPH C permanent-magnet hysteresis measurement brochure
claims: NdFeB characterization includes remanence/coercivity/energy product; optional heated measurement up to 200 °C. Rare-earth saturation needs separate pulse magnetizer. Poles use soft magnetic steel or FeCo options.

sources.title: Magnetic Instrumentation company and contact
claims: Manufacturer offers built-to-order magnetizing systems; contact and laboratory Indianapolis. Official inspected pages do not explicitly identify the model assembly factory.

sources.title: Magnetic Instrumentation Model 3000
claims: 3000-1: 8500 J at 3000 V, 1890 µF bank. Model family uses oil-filled capacitors, SCR output and NEMA 12 enclosure; page gives differing input options, so none converted to kW.
